bench.lede: This page is for checking how the side panel works with a keyboard, a screen reader and on a phone. It shows no figures.
panel.label: Figure details
panel.tab_error: We could not load this section. Try again in a few seconds.
panel.body.fuente: Where the figure comes from will go here: for a reported figure, the filing, tag, period and filing date; for an estimate, the run, its cut-off date and the source of each assumption.
panel.body.formula: The calculation's steps will go here, with the formula you would type in your spreadsheet.
panel.body.concepto: What the figure means will go here, for example what net debt is.
panel.body.ysi: Here you will be able to change a model assumption and see what moves. A reported figure cannot be edited.
panel.body.leer: Headlines published before the cut-off date, and related companies, will go here.

card.ask.reader_unsure: I'm not sure I understood your question. Check the reading or choose from the menus.
card.ask.company_missing: Which company do you mean? Warren covers eight: {companies}.
card.ask.value_range: You wrote a range ({text}) for {input}. Which value do you want to try, or would you rather see the sensitivity table?
card.ask.value_missing: Which value do you want to try for {input}? You can also see the sensitivity table.
card.ask.value_missing_via: How big is the Fed's move? Write it in basis points.
card.ask.value_ambiguous: Is “{text}” {first} or {second}? Some countries use the point for thousands and others for decimals.
card.ask.value_unreadable: I couldn't read the value “{text}” for {input}. Write it as a number.
card.ask.driver_periods: Do you change {input} for next year only, or for every forecast year?
card.ask.method_unknown: Warren computes the terminal value with its own method or with Gordon's; it has no exit-multiple method. Which one do you want?
card.note.corte_default: Cutoff date: {date}. Warren uses only what was published up to that day, the last one that has ended in New York (today is {today}). You can pick an earlier date to see what was known then.
card.note.corte_from_question: Cutoff date: {date}, the one I read in your question. Please confirm it.
card.note.fed_move_is_event: The value is the Fed's move, not the risk-free rate's. Warren turns it into a change in the 10-year Treasury yield with a range from published studies, never one for one.
card.note.cash_unchanged: You change only the shares outstanding: the cash that would be paid or received stays the same. So value per share moves without anyone paying or receiving anything, which does not happen in real life. For a buyback, change debt: Warren adjusts the shares with it.
card.note.wacc_bypasses_parts: With WACC set directly, Warren stops using its components: beta, the risk-free rate, the equity risk premium, the cost of debt, the tax shield and the weights of debt and equity.
card.note.usd_only: Warren reports in US dollars, as these companies file their financial statements. It doesn't convert currencies.
card.note.intrinsic_value_offer: Warren doesn't forecast prices or say whether to buy. I'll show you its intrinsic value, its range and which assumptions it depends on.
card.note.intrinsic_value_offer_target: Warren doesn't compute a target price or say whether to buy. I'll show you its intrinsic value, its range and which assumptions it depends on.
input.debt_tax_rate: the tax rate on the debt tax shield
card.ask.value_currency: You wrote “{text}” in another currency. Warren doesn't convert currencies: write the amount in US dollars.
card.ask.percent_or_points: You wrote “{text}” for {input}. Is that percentage points (say, from 20% to 10%) or a share of its level (from 20% to 18%)?
card.ask.points_or_bp: You wrote “{text}” for {input}. Is that percentage points or basis points (100 bp = 1 point)?
card.ask.fed_surprise: Does the Fed's move surprise the market, or was it expected? What was expected is already in the bond yield on the cutoff date and barely moves it; only the unexpected part does.
card.ask.wacc_and_parts: You set WACC and also change one of its components. With WACC fixed, that change would have no effect. Which do you want to use?
card.note.relative_change: I read “{text}” as a relative change in {input}: a share of its current level, not percentage points.

answer.title: {company} revenue: the next four quarters
answer.reading.label: How I read your question
answer.fx.empty: Pick a figure to see its formula
answer.table.caption: Revenue forecast by quarter, US$ millions
answer.table.range_sub: the actual figure fell inside 8 times in 10
answer.table.closed: Ended, but {company} has not published the figure yet: Warren forecasts it
answer.sure.title: How sure?
answer.coverage.all: of the ranges held the actual figure (8 companies)
answer.coverage.company: of {company}'s ranges held the actual figure
answer.sure.body: Each case is a one-quarter forecast Warren made on a past date, compared later with the figure the company reported. A p10–p90 range (10th to 90th percentile) should hold the actual figure about 8 times in 10. These shares are not the chance that this forecast is right: they say whether the ranges are as wide as they should be. A little over 80% means they are a little wider than needed. The forecast uses only the company's filings, not recent news.
answer.chart.title: Reported and forecast
answer.chart.aria: {company} quarterly revenue in US$ millions: {reported} reported quarters and {forecast} forecast with their p10–p90 range. The forecasts and their ranges are in the table.
answer.chart.source: Source: Warren's baseline forecast, estimate of {date}. Revenue reported in {company}'s 10-K and 10-Q filed by that date. Range: the same forecast's past misses, known on that date. Estimate:
formula.revenue_from_growth_vs_year_earl: revenue of the same quarter a year earlier (B), times (1 + the average annual growth of the last three fiscal years, C). It is Warren's baseline forecast, not the DCF.
answer.fuente.run_line: Estimate of {date} ({run_id}). It uses only filings {company} made with the SEC by that date:
answer.fuente.derived_q4: The 10-K's fiscal year less its first three quarters
answer.fuente.not_recorded: This estimate did not store its source.
answer.fuente.same_filing: Each growth rate uses both years as one filing reports them, so the figures are measured the same way. US$ millions.
answer.fuente.range_how: the forecast times (1 + the miss percentile), from the misses this same forecast made in the past across the 8 companies at the same number of quarters ahead ({n} misses).
answer.fuente.range_known: Misses known on {date}, from actual figures filed by {filed_to}.
answer.fuente.range_foot: The range shows how far the baseline forecast has missed before; it does not include news or other shocks, so it is not the whole uncertainty.
answer.fuente.coverage_how: of {n} past cases, the actual figure fell inside the range in {inside}, below it in {below} and above it in {above}.
answer.fuente.coverage_interval: 90% confidence interval for that share: {low} to {high}.
answer.fuente.coverage_foot: Forecasts made since {since}, each with only what was known on its date.
answer.table.season: Each forecast starts from the same quarter a year earlier, so the company's seasons stay: its biggest quarter stays on top.
answer.kpi.all: of the ranges held the actual figure: {inside} of {n} cases across the 8 companies
answer.kpi.company: of {company}'s ranges held the actual figure: {inside} of {n} cases
answer.fuente.rounding: In the sheet, C goes in as a fraction with six decimals; the screen rounds it to one decimal.
cells.title: The cells behind the answer
cells.years.label: Years of history
cells.years.note: The years of history only change the charts: the assumption always uses the last three fiscal years.
cells.derived_title: Computed: the 10-K's fiscal year minus its first three quarters
cells.derived_note: * The fourth quarter has no quarterly filing: it is the 10-K's fiscal year minus its first three quarters.
cells.soon.body: which products and regions moved this revenue. Warren does not read that split from the filings yet.
cells.source: Source: Warren's baseline forecast, estimate of {date}; history from {company}'s 10-Ks and 10-Qs filed by that date.
cells.plain.no_chart: This cell has no chart on this screen yet.
cells.b.title: Revenue in the same fiscal quarter, a year earlier
cells.b.lead: The base of each forecast. It is a reported figure, not an assumption.
cells.b.aria: {quarter}: revenue in the same quarter over {n} fiscal years, from {low} to {high} US$ millions; the base is {base} and the forecast {forecast}.
cells.b.caption: Each chart is one fiscal quarter over several years.
cells.b.scale: All use the same scale, from {low} to {high} US$ millions.
cells.b.note: Each quarter is forecast from the same quarter a year earlier because sales follow the seasons: comparing a quarter with the one before would mix season with growth.
cells.b.table_caption: Revenue in the same quarter by fiscal year, US$ millions
cells.c.title: Annual revenue growth
cells.c.lead_end: in each of the next four quarters, against the same quarter a year earlier.
cells.c.lead_fading_end: , against the same quarter a year earlier; later ones move toward long-term growth.
cells.c.annual_title: By fiscal year: the assumption is the average of the last three
cells.c.annual_aria: {company}'s annual revenue growth, fiscal years {first} to {last}: {values}. The assumption, {assumption}, is the average of {used}.
cells.c.quarterly_title: By quarter, against the same quarter a year earlier
cells.c.quarterly_aria: Each quarter's growth against the same quarter a year earlier, from {first} to {last}, and the {assumption} assumption in the four forecast quarters. The figures are in the table.
cells.c.note_recent: The three latest quarters grew {values}; the assumption is {assumption}.
cells.c.note_rule: Warren does not say whether that pace will last or stop: its baseline is a simple, fixed rule, the average of the last three full fiscal years, which leaves single quarters out on purpose so that one period does not move it.
cells.c.note_next_year: Fiscal year {year} enters the average once {company} files its annual report.
cells.c.note_sure: How well this rule has done is above, in “How sure?”.
cells.c.table_caption: Revenue growth by fiscal year and by quarter
cells.fuente.known_on: As known on {date}: the figure in the latest filing made by that day.
cells.fuente.history_foot: US$ millions. History: it does not enter the calculation, except the base and the averaged years.
cells.fuente.growth_how: Revenue of {now} against {before}: revenue ÷ revenue a year earlier − 1.
cells.fuente.growth_foot: US$ millions. The percentage is rounded to one decimal.
cells.fuente.assumption_lead: The growth Warren assumes for the next four quarters, against the same quarter a year earlier.
cells.fx.reported: Reported figure: Warren applies no formula to it.
cells.fx.derived: 10-K fiscal year − Q1 − Q2 − Q3 (computed by Warren from the filings).
cells.intro_lead: Each forecast in the table comes from two cells of the formula:
cells.intro_rest: B is revenue in the same fiscal quarter a year earlier; C is the growth Warren assumes. For each: how it moved in recent years and what Warren assumes now.
